encryption.experimentalHelp: This feature has not had an outside security review yet. Do not rely on it to protect sensitive conversations.
encryption.trust: An encrypted chat is only as safe as every device in it. Anyone who controls one of your devices, or one of {name}'s, can read it.
encryption.trustYou: An encrypted chat is only as safe as every device in it. Anyone who controls one of your devices, or a device of the person you chat with, can read it.
encryption.webLimit: In a browser, the server you use also sends the app's code. Encryption here keeps out the IRC network, a stolen server database and a curious operator, but not an operator who sends changed code. The desktop app does not have this limit.
encryption.storageLimit: Your keys and your encrypted history are stored only in this browser. Clearing its site data deletes them, and they cannot be recovered.

blocked.notDirect: Encryption works in direct messages only.
blocked.network: Encryption works between people on this IRCord server, on its own network.
blocked.selfAccount: Log in to an account on this network to use encryption.
blocked.peerAccount: {name} is not logged in to an account on this network.
blocked.peerNoKeys: {name} has not set up encryption yet.
blocked.deviceNotReady: Set up encryption on this device first.
blocked.bot: Bots cannot take part in encrypted chats.

dialog.intro: Messages you send from now on are encrypted on this device. Only your devices and {name}'s can read them. The server stores only ciphertext.
dialog.noAccept: {name} does not need to accept. Their app shows that you turned on encryption, and either of you can turn it off again.
dialog.lost: In this chat, link previews, server search and message text in push notifications stop working.
dialog.askText: I'd like to use an encrypted chat with you. Open Settings → Encryption in IRCord to set it up.
dialog.on: Messages in this chat are end-to-end encrypted.
dialog.verifyHelp: Compare this code with the one on {name}'s screen, in person or over another channel you trust. If they match, nobody is between you. One verification covers all of their devices.
dialog.scanMismatch: The codes do not match. Do not mark {name} as verified.
dialog.turnOffBody: New messages will be sent unencrypted. {name} sees that you turned it off. Messages sent so far stay encrypted.
dialog.codeFailed: The security code is not available yet.

event.onPeer: {name} turned on end-to-end encryption. Messages from here on can only be read on your devices and {name}'s.

message.ownLost: You sent this from this device, but its copy is no longer stored here.
message.unreadable: This encrypted message cannot be read on this device.
message.notApproved: Approve this device to read encrypted messages.
message.beforeDevice: This message was encrypted before this device could read it. It stays readable on your other devices.
message.wrongConversation: This encrypted message belongs to another conversation. It is not shown here.
message.senderMismatch: This message did not come from the account that sent it. It is not shown.
message.identityChanged: The sender's keys changed. Accept the change to read new messages.
message.notEncryptedHelp: This message arrived without encryption in an encrypted chat. It may come from another IRC client, or someone else could have added it.
message.actionUnavailable: In an encrypted chat, you can reply to, react to and edit only encrypted messages this device can read.
message.fileFailed: The file could not be decrypted.

composer.approveFirst: Approve this device to send encrypted messages.
composer.notReady: Encryption is not ready on this device yet.
composer.rawBlocked: Your chat with {name} is encrypted. Send the message in that chat, or turn off encryption first.
composer.plainUpload: This file was uploaded without encryption. Attach it again.

reset.title: {name} started fresh with new encryption keys.
reset.body: Earlier messages stay readable here, but {name}'s new devices cannot read them. This is expected if {name} lost their devices. It would look the same if someone got into {name}'s account or the server interfered. If you are not sure, ask {name} another way.
reset.acknowledgeFirst: {name} has new encryption keys. Read the notice in your chat and select OK to continue.

banner.plaintext: A message arrived without encryption in this encrypted chat. It is marked “Not encrypted”.
banner.approve: This chat is encrypted. Approve this device to read and send messages here.
banner.resetElsewhere: Encryption was reset from another device. This device cannot read new encrypted messages until it is approved again.

settings.intro: End-to-end encrypted direct messages. Keys live only on your devices: there is no recovery key and no backup on the server.

state.off: The server does not offer encryption.
state.unsupported: This browser cannot store encryption keys. It needs IndexedDB, Web Locks and Web Workers.
state.waiting: Waiting for the connection to the home network.
state.needsApproval: This device needs approval from another of your devices before it can read encrypted chats.
state.resetElsewhere: Encryption was reset from another device. Approve this device again, or start fresh.
state.ready: Ready. This device can read and send encrypted messages.
state.readyIdentity: Ready. This device holds your account's identity key and can approve your other devices.

settings.devicesHelp: Each device has its own keys. A removed device cannot read messages sent after its removal.
settings.removeBody: It can no longer read new encrypted messages. Messages it already has stay on it.
settings.approveHelp: Sign in on the new device and open Settings → Encryption there. Then scan its code here.
settings.approveNeedsIdentity: Only the device that set up encryption first can approve other devices in this version.
settings.startFreshHelp: Use this only when no approved device is left, or when one was stolen.
settings.startFreshBody: Your account gets a new security identity. This device cannot read earlier encrypted messages. Everyone you chat with encrypted sees a notice and must verify you again. Your other devices lose their approval.
settings.secondDevice: Your encrypted history exists only on your devices. Approve a second device so that losing this one does not lose it.
settings.lastDeviceSignOut: This is your only device that can read your encrypted chats. Logging out deletes its keys and its encrypted history for good.

approval.requestHelp: On a device that already has encryption, open Settings → Encryption and scan this code.
approval.noCamera: No camera? Type this code there:
approval.keepSecret: Keep this code to yourself. Someone who sees it could try to get their own device approved in place of this one.
approval.scanUnavailable: This browser cannot scan codes. Type the code instead.
approval.typeCode: Or type the 20-digit code shown on the new device
approval.waitingCount: {count} device is waiting for approval. | {count} devices are waiting for approval.
approval.pendingNone: No device is waiting. Open Settings → Encryption on the new device first.
approval.badCode: Enter all 20 digits of the code.
approval.notFound: No waiting device has this code. Check the code, or open it on the new device again.
approval.approving: Approving and adding the device to your encrypted chats…
approval.failed: The device could not be approved: {reason}

scanner.label: Camera view for scanning a code

search.local: Encrypted chats are searched on this device only.
